slides.headline: America's most famous moment never happened like this.

slides.text: Philadelphia, 1776. The draft of the Declaration of Independence is presented to Congress. You have probably seen this scene on the two-dollar bill.

slides.headline: The committee
slides.text: In the centre stand the five men who drafted it: John Adams, Roger Sherman, Robert Livingston, Thomas Jefferson and Benjamin Franklin.

slides.headline: Jefferson
slides.text: Thomas Jefferson, the tall man with red hair, hands over the document he mostly wrote himself. He was only 33.

slides.headline: Franklin
slides.text: Beside him stands Benjamin Franklin, the oldest man in the room, calm and patient, waiting for the vote.

slides.headline: Never like this
slides.text: But this moment never happened like this. These men were never all together in one room on a single day.

slides.headline: From life
slides.text: Trumbull painted most faces from life, travelling for years to find them. Some men he could not find were simply left out.

slides.headline: The Capitol
slides.text: This huge canvas, more than five metres wide, has hung in the Rotunda of the US Capitol since 1826.

slides.headline: True enough?
slides.text: A real event, but an invented scene. Does a painting have to be accurate to become history?
